title: Quick Accent conficts with Keyboard Manager remaps

status.label: Retest after the shipped Quick Accent injection fix
status.detail: The last confirmation was on 0.100.2. PowerToys 0.102.3001 includes PR #48572, which tags Quick Accent-injected Backspace events so Keyboard Manager ignores them.

judgment.rationale: The original report says Quick Accent's synthetic Backspace becomes the remapped slash when Backspace is swapped with another key. A later commenter confirmed the issue on 0.100.2 when Backspace is remapped, and a maintainer asked whether it persists on 0.100.2 or above. Since then, merged PR #48572 added dwExtraInfo=0x110 to Quick Accent's synthetic Backspace events; bit 0x1 is Keyboard Manager's explicit injected-event ignore flag, and that commit is included in current release v0.102.3001. The source change is a strong likely fix, but the issue has no post-release confirmation. Ask for the exact sequence on the current release rather than proposing a duplicate code change.
evidence: The issue's PowerToys 0.82 repro swaps Backspace with slash, activates Quick Accent, and reports that deleting the original character inserts slash instead.
A later commenter reports the issue still on PowerToys 0.100.2 and says it appears limited to users who remap Backspace.
In current source, PowerAccent.Core/Tools/WindowsFunctions.cs tags synthetic VK_BACK input with 0x110.
CommonSharedConstants::KEYBOARDMANAGER_INJECTED_FLAG is 0x1, and KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp's GeneratedByKBM ignores events carrying that flag.
Merged PR #48572 adds the tag to Quick Accent input injection and is included in release v0.102.3001.
The issue remains open with four comments and no assignees; the current-release retest is unanswered.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether the original Backspace-remap/Quick Accent sequence still inserts the remapped key on v0.102.3001, which includes the likely fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: A likely correction is already shipped in v0.102.3001: Quick Accent marks synthetic Backspace as a Keyboard Manager-ignored event. Do not propose another fix until the reporter confirms whether this release resolves the exact scenario.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent's synthetic Backspace reportedly becomes a remapped slash when Backspace is remapped; a likely injection-marker fix has since shipped and needs validation.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.82 and remapping Backspace to slash.
The report says choosing an accented character causes slash to be inserted instead of deleting the original character.
A commenter reported the same issue on 0.100.2 when Backspace is remapped.
PR #48572 added the 0x110 injection tag to Quick Accent's synthetic keyboard events; this contains the Keyboard Manager ignore bit 0x1 and is included in v0.102.3001.
inferences: The shipped injection tag should prevent Keyboard Manager from translating Quick Accent's synthetic Backspace, but the issue has not been retested after that change.
issue_context.analysis: Current source aligns with the reported failure path: Quick Accent synthesizes VK_BACK, and Keyboard Manager has an explicit flag for ignoring injected input. The merged change marks those events, making the latest release a discriminating retest. Wait for that result before suggesting another code change.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body and all four comments, including the 0.100.2 confirmation and minimized question about newer builds.
Inspected PowerAccent.Core/Tools/WindowsFunctions.cs and KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp for the injected-key marker and ignore path.
Verified PR #48572 is merged and its commit is included in tag v0.102.3001.

information_gaps.information: Whether Quick Accent still inserts the remapped slash instead of deleting the original character on PowerToys v0.102.3001 with Backspace remapped
information_gaps.why_needed: The latest release includes a change that marks Quick Accent's synthetic Backspace as input Keyboard Manager must ignore; the original behavior was last confirmed on 0.100.2.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On v0.102.3001, remap Backspace to slash, activate Quick Accent, choose an accent, and report whether the original character is deleted or slash is inserted.

actions.label: Retest Quick Accent with the current Backspace-remap fix

comment.body: Thanks for confirming this on PowerToys 0.100.2 when Backspace is remapped. Since v0.102.3001 includes PR #48572's Quick Accent input-injection change, could you retest the same Backspace-to-slash plus Quick Accent sequence on v0.102.3001 and confirm whether it still inserts `/` instead of deleting the original character?
